NO. 014 · Songbirds & City Birds / Turdidae · Thrushes

Chinese Blackbird

乌鸫 · wū dōng Turdus mandarinus
Resident Common 24–28 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

A black suit, and the best voice in town

At first glance a black bird; look again and there is a golden eye-ring and an orange-yellow bill. The Chinese Blackbird is the tenor of southern cities: on a March morning it stands on a rooftop or a treetop and sings the whole street quiet.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • MaleAll black, orange-yellow bill, a ring of golden skin around the eye, dark brown legs. In sunlight the black takes on a fine blue-grey sheen.
  • FemaleDark brown above, paler and finely streaked on the throat, bill duller and often brownish.
  • JuvenileBrown with heavy spotting on the breast, very unlike the adult and often taken for another species.
  • ShapeRound and sturdy, fairly long-tailed; hops on the ground and stands upright when it stops.

Behaviour

Usually turning over lawns and leaf litter for earthworms and insects, and eating berries. Strongly territorial when breeding, chasing birds larger than itself and even cats. The deep cup nest is reinforced with mud inside and hidden in a fork, on a wall or in a trellis. The city population is resident all year — one of the few songbirds that gives a concert in every season.

Voice

Field recording
Tap the waveform to seek · headphones recommended
0:00 / 0:15
Recording iNaturalist user skystargazer · Licence CC BY-NC · Original file

A fluent, long, highly musical song, often ending with mimicry of other birds or even phone ringtones, delivered solo from a high perch at dawn and dusk. The call is a sharp 'chook-chook-chook' or a thin 'tseee', repeated when alarmed.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • SYSU Zhuhai Campus
  • Xiangshan Lake Park understorey
  • Banzhang Hill
  • campus lawns
Field note
A solo with real melody, complete phrases and a little improvisation is almost certainly a blackbird. The bird singing loudly at night in the city is usually this species too, confused by street lighting.
